clue.text: Oppose company producing cosmetic preparation

blocks.note: to face an opponent is to confront or oppose them
a pack is a group or company, as of wolves or scouts

explanation.surface: A firm takes a stand against a rival business over some beauty product.
explanation.definitionFit: A face pack is a paste spread over the skin and left to dry, a standard beauty treatment.

clue.text: Deceptive fault under ground

indicators.note: something ground is crushed into pieces, so these letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A misleading geological fault lying beneath the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as soil beneath a fault line, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraudulent means dishonest and intended to trick people, so it describes something deceptive.

clue.text: Pain in neck, alien insect

blocks.note: a crick is a painful stiffness of the neck
ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: An annoying creature from another world, like a pest from outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pain in neck' suggests a nuisance, but it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a chirping, jumping insect related to the grasshopper.

clue.text: Colour scheme set up in perfect operation

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word reads from bottom to top
in puts the turned word inside the other one

blocks.note: pure means flawless or perfect
decor is a room's style of colour and furnishing

explanation.surface: A decorator's colours are arranged in a flawless piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is an established way of carrying something out, and in medicine an operation.

clue.text: Poet, eccentric lady, can run off

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are put into an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet, an odd woman, is able to dash away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady' hints at a female poet, which she is; 'run off' could also suggest printing copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol Ann Duffy is a Scottish writer who served as the UK's Poet Laureate from 2009 to 2019.

clue.text: In course of fever balderdash is spoken

indicators.note: something found in the course of a phrase lies partway through it, running across the word boundary

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A patient with a high temperature talks nonsense, as a delirious person might.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbal means expressed in words, especially said aloud rather than written down, as in a verbal agreement.

clue.text: Heron for example regarding middle of water

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central character, the only one kept

blocks.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
re means regarding, as in a letter heading
the central letter of the five

explanation.surface: A wading bird is mentioned in connection with the water it stands in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heron for example' reads as heron being the example, but the definition is just Heron.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a kind of heron, usually white, with long plumes in breeding season.

clue.text: Book about soldier nearly made into TV western series

indicators.note: nearly means almost all, so the last letter of the word is cut

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
on means about, as in a talk on a topic
an Anzac is a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps

explanation.surface: A book about a soldier gets adapted for a cowboy show on television.
explanation.walkthrough: ANZAC loses its final C; the Anzacs fought famously at Gallipoli in 1915.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonanza was a long-running American television western about the Cartwright family's Ponderosa ranch.

clue.text: Do nothing for portion of bread

blocks.note: first meaning: to idle or lounge about
second meaning: a shaped mass of baked dough

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests working for a crust; the verb and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to laze idly as a verb, and as a noun a single baked unit of bread.

clue.text: Friend mostly surrounded by work

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: amid means in the middle of, surrounded by
a machine that works is one that goes

explanation.surface: A colleague who is nearly always found among the job at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrounded by work' reads as one idea, but 'by' belongs with 'surrounded' and 'work' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for a pal, borrowed into casual English speech as a matey term of address.

clue.text: Direct, objective answer in votes

blocks.note: to refer someone somewhere is to direct them there
an end is an aim or objective
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A plain, straightforward reply is given in a series of ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda is a plural of referendum, a public vote on a single question put to the whole electorate.

clue.text: In essence, supply word of assent and agree

blocks.note: to fund is to supply with money
amen is said to show agreement, as at a prayer's end
figures that tally agree with each other

explanation.surface: Basically, give a word of approval and go along with things.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentally means at the most basic level, at heart, which is what 'in essence' expresses.

clue.text: Jazz pianist liked long tune to play

indicators.note: putting words to play suggests toying with them freely, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written: thirteen letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist enjoyed taking a lengthy melody and performing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington was the American bandleader, composer and pianist behind 'Take the A Train' and many swing standards.

clue.text: Criminal receiving elevation, man in strong position

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the first word holds the following ones inside it

blocks.note: bad as in wicked or criminal
a ridge is a raised stretch of ground
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A crook gets promoted and becomes a powerful figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a fortified position seized on the enemy's side of a river, a military foothold.

clue.text: Country I haunt, wretchedly in trouble after revolution

indicators.note: something done wretchedly is done badly, so these letters come out in a poor, jumbled order
a revolution turns something round, so this word is read from its end back to its start
in places the jumbled letters inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A ghost confesses to miserable hauntings in a land troubled after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters sit inside LIA, which is AIL turned round; 'revolution' reads like a political uprising, apt for a Baltic state.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuania is a Baltic nation in northern Europe, bordering Latvia, Belarus and Poland.

clue.text: Just accepting learner's ability

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: just and fair both mean impartial
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A trainee's talent being simply acknowledged.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural talent or aptitude for something, close in sense to a knack or gift.

clue.text: Following hesitation over treatment of rat I go to get pest controller

indicators.note: a treatment processes material, so these letters are worked into another order

blocks.note: f. abbreviates following, as in page references
um is the sound of hesitating
taken as written

explanation.surface: After some hesitation about dealing with a rat, a pest controller is sent for.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first pieces above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A fumigator uses smoke or gas to clear a building of vermin and insects.

clue.text: Relative insider, chef dispensing with regular ingredients

indicators.note: throwing out components at a regular interval leaves every other character standing

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters are kept

explanation.surface: A kitchen insider, a chef cutting back on the usual ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen language of ingredients misleads: here ingredients are the letters themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, one of the family members a person counts among their kin.

clue.text: Concise saying from end of fable on two farm animals

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final character, the one kept here

blocks.note: the final letter
a pig and a ram

explanation.surface: A pithy moral at the close of a tale about a pair of farmyard beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Aesop or Animal Farm; the two animals are a pig and a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty remark or pointed saying, often memorable for its brevity.

clue.text: Blissful place, Italian city, not one gripped by fear

indicators.note: not one tells us to take away the letter standing for the numeral one
being gripped means being held inside, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: dread is great fear
Milan is the city in northern Italy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A happy destination, an Italian city, is not somewhere anyone fears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not one gripped by fear' sounds like nobody is afraid; in fact the city drops its one and is then held by fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamland is an idyllic imaginary world, or the state of sleep, both pictured as places of bliss.

clue.text: Wrongly ban item of electronic music

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters are in an incorrect order and must be put right

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wrongly prohibiting a track of electronic music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient is a genre of atmospheric, slow electronic music pioneered by Brian Eno.

clue.text: Ace goes into lead, being fit, unusually tireless

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters fall into an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
taken as written

explanation.surface: A star player takes the lead, being fit and remarkably tireless.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter is added to the other words and the whole lot is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefatigable describes someone who never grows weary, persisting untiringly however long the effort lasts.

clue.text: Urgent to include grand mournful song

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: a dire need is an urgent one
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: An urgent request to put a grand mourning song on the programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow lament sung at a funeral or for the dead.

clue.text: Exploits raised in quarrel

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the word reads from the bottom

blocks.note: to tap a resource is to exploit it

explanation.surface: Heroic deeds being brought up in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' looks like a noun for deeds, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel or minor squabble, typically brief.

clue.text: Depiction of beam in doorway

indicators.note: in places one word inside another, here within the frame of the doorway

blocks.note: a portal is a grand doorway or gateway
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A painting of light shining through an open door.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a representation of someone or something, in art, words or acting.

clue.text: Subject covered by Goethe methodically

indicators.note: something covered by these words lies concealed within them, spanning the gap

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the poet's name and the next word

explanation.surface: A topic the German writer Goethe treated in a systematic way.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or main idea of a work, discussion or talk.

clue.text: Agent satisfied about mood

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent or representative
a demand that is satisfied has been met

explanation.surface: A salesperson pleased with how someone is feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' but turns the joined pieces round.
explanation.definitionFit: Temper is a person's state of mind or humour, as in 'in a good temper'.

clue.text: Hot yard deserved to be supplied with water

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
YD is the standard abbreviation for yard
something that rated a mention deserved one

explanation.surface: A sweltering garden plot has earned a good watering.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrated means having absorbed or been given enough fluid, from the Greek root for liquid.
